economy.summary: In a 2024 pre-election interview he supported the state Senate's plan to reduce the personal income tax and eliminate the gross receipts tax on electricity; these are tax measures he framed as relief for residents.
economy.short: Supported reducing personal income tax, ending electricity gross receipts tax.

taxes.summary: Criticized the 2026-27 state budget, saying the $50.8 billion plan is not balanced, relies on $2.6 billion in deferred payments that mask true spending levels, and will lead to a future tax increase.
taxes.short: Says state budget overspends, is not balanced, risks tax increase.

abortion.summary: Opposed House Bill 1957 in December 2025, saying he was stunned that a majority of House colleagues would support what he called abortion on demand until the birth of a child, and stating that aborting a child that has reached viability is murder.
abortion.short: Opposed 2025 abortion bill; says post-viability abortion is murder.

education.summary: Questions the size of recent increases in state K-12 education funding, saying per-pupil spending in Pennsylvania is well above the national average; as a member of the state university system's board he supported keeping tuition frozen.
education.short: Questions K-12 funding increases; supported freezing state university tuition.

energy.summary: Co-sponsored 2019 legislation (House Bill 2025) requiring that any state measure to tax or impose fees on carbon dioxide emissions, such as the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative carbon pricing program, be submitted to the General Assembly rather than enacted by regulation.
energy.short: Co-sponsored bill requiring legislative review of carbon emissions taxes.

guns.summary: Says he has supported the right to own and bear arms since first taking office, citing what he describes as a 100 percent gun-rights voting record and an NRA endorsement.
guns.short: Supports gun rights; cites his voting record and NRA endorsement.

economy.summary: His platform calls for more resources to repair aging infrastructure, saying bridges are rusting and crumbling and water and power systems are outdated, with repairs creating local jobs, and for building up Pennsylvania-based local industries.
economy.short: Proposes infrastructure repairs to create jobs; supports local industries.

taxes.summary: His platform proposes tax cuts and grants for Pennsylvania-based businesses and agriculture to encourage community growth.
taxes.short: Proposes tax cuts, grants for Pennsylvania businesses and agriculture.

education.summary: His platform supports shifting away from standardized testing and back to teaching critical thinking, with appropriate tax funding for public schools.
education.short: Supports less standardized testing, critical thinking, public school funding.

healthcare.summary: His platform calls for lowering prescription medication costs and improving drug pricing transparency, while protecting community health centers and rural hospitals.
healthcare.short: Proposes lowering drug costs; protecting rural hospitals, health centers.

energy.summary: Has proposed converting Woodcock Lake Park in Crawford County into a state park, saying state management would improve maintenance of the area's natural resources and bring revenue and tourism; this is a parks proposal, and he has not detailed a broader energy or environmental platform.
energy.short: Proposes making Woodcock Lake Park a state park.
